chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the pre-seminal fluid (al-madhy) that flows until it reaches the thigh. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not break one's prayer, nor is it required to wash it from the thigh, because it has not exited from the exit of the semen. It is merely in the status of mucus.'

key_terms.النُّخَامَةِ: Mucus/phlegm, used here as an analogy for the nature of madhy
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: Pre-seminal fluid, a clear viscous fluid released during arousal
key_terms.الْمَنِيِّ: Semen, the thicker fluid released during orgasm, which has different ruling
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهُ: To wash it (referring to the fluid from the body/clothes)

ai.seo_question: Does pre-seminal fluid (madhy) break prayer or require washing in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes al-madhy from semen (mani) by noting its origin is not the primary reproductive exit, thereby classifying it as minor impurity (najis al-athar) rather than major impurity. This ruling simplifies ritual purity for worshippers, as it does not break the prayer nor require full washing (ghusl), aligning with the principle that fluids not expelled from the semen's specific channel are treated like phlegm. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for differentiating between the purification requirements of madhy and mani.
